tagline: One of Poland's oldest cities has a colourful Renaissance market square where two mechanical goats butt heads at noon, a cathedral island and a lively student scene.
overview: Poznań, halfway between Berlin and Warsaw, is one of the cradles of the Polish state: the first Polish rulers were based on Ostrów Tumski, its cathedral island, more than 1,000 years ago, and Poland's first rulers are buried in the cathedral.

The Old Market Square is ringed by narrow, brightly painted merchant houses and centred on the Renaissance Town Hall. Every day at noon two mechanical goats emerge above the clock and butt heads twelve times, a scene tied to a local legend.

Poznań is a busy trade-fair and university city, so it feels young and lively. Try rogal świętomarciński, a croissant filled with white poppy seeds made for St Martin's Day, and visit the Imperial Castle, the Croissant Museum or the lakes of Malta and Rusałka.
